title: Let only the station turn a token back into a card number

blocks.text: This picks up where the previous practice ended: `src/main/java/com/example/practice/TokenVault.java` already contains its solution. The vault issues good tokens now, but a penetration test of the whole platform reported this:

items: with the pharmacy app's own credentials, the testers got card numbers back for every token in its database;
the cinema's integration sent a pharmacy token with a cinema purchase, and the pharmacy's customer was charged;
a made-up token ended in a `NullPointerException` instead of a refusal the station could answer;
a customer who removed his saved card was charged with it weeks later.

blocks.text: Finish `detokenize` and `revoke`, the two methods marked `TODO`. The comments say what each must achieve. The station, the component that builds the request for the network, calls `detokenize` with its permissions and the requestor it is acting for. About ten lines in total.

cases.says: a caller with the DETOKENIZE permission, acting for the token's requestor, gets the card number back
a caller without the DETOKENIZE permission is refused with a SecurityException, whatever else it may do
a token presented for a requestor it was not issued to is refused with an ISOException
a token the vault never issued is refused with an ISOException, not answered with nothing
a revoked token no longer leads to its card
after a revoke the requestor's card gets a new token, and other requestors' tokens stay as they are

origin.section: 14.5. Only the Component That Builds the Network Message May Turn a Token Back Into a Card Number

concepts: Only the station that builds the network message may detokenize, for the token's own requestor; unknown, revoked or foreign tokens are refused before anything reaches the issuer, and a revoked card gets a new token.
